chipSemantics.paths: Same bridge exposes CPU+accurate S-DSP SpcCore and DSP-only SnesDspCore. Fixed 32000-Hz native stereo Float32; 1024-native-frame bridge block. No optional fast DSP, sound filter, tempo adjustment or surround disabling. Default two-byte IPL fallback only.
chipSemantics.snapshot: snapshot() copies 65536 RAM and 128 DSP bytes plus nativeFrames. It omits CPU/timers/envelopes/BRR/FIFO/echo phase, so it is observational data, not complete continuation state. No JS native-state save/load export. SPC restart reloads original file bytes and retains mute; DSP reset clears RAM/registers and retains mute.
chipSemantics.mute: Separate voice-output mask suppresses dry mix and new echo sends without KOFF or freezing voice state. Existing echo tails remain audible; altered echo RAM means muted progression is not the unmuted trajectory.
chipSemantics.trace: Fresh loaded unmuted CPU SPC only; up to 1000000 ordered four-uint32 DSP/RAM records and 600 seconds at effective DSP clock 1024000. Coalesces same-address RAM writes between DSP advancement. Optional 65536-byte RAM read mask from identical discovery pass filters only CPU working RAM. Limit errors reject capture; original PCM retained.
chipSemantics.observer: Loaded CPU SPC can start bounded 16..8192 DSP-write observation at current frame; four uint32 words carry low/high absolute clock and register/value. drainDspEventsInto emits owned Float64 triples and takeDspEventOverflow resets lost count. Overflow does not stop/alter playback. Independent from offline tracing.
chipSemantics.timeline: DSP-only immutable copied initial RAM/DSP and ordered events; frames exactly durationClocks/32 with upstream four-frame initial FIFO. Replay omits SPC700 CPU; valid only for recorded interval and original RAM access assumptions. Events at subframe effective DSP clocks preserved; not arbitrary mid-song restoration.
chipSemantics.localAdaptations: Unsigned register-dispatch predicates avoid signed negative-shift UB; sample directory addresses wrap to 16 bits; output mute, offline trace, observer and per-instance DSP RAM read hooks retained unchanged.

reports.frameCountScope: All bounded nonzero PCM render requests go through one counter, including wrapper/trace positives, scenarios/probes, failed attempts and timeline-end silence. Internal 1024-frame chunks are not added again; failed trace rendering may advance native state before rejecting delivery, and ended timeline silence does not advance nativeFrames.

sourceFacts: The existing test resolves fetching when its custom fetch is invoked, then awaits player.close() and the initialization rejection before checking state after 180 ms.
Initialization awaits a context resume before starting delayed WASM fetch and AudioWorklet addModule in parallel.
The AudioWorkletNode is constructed only after both operations complete successfully and signal.throwIfAborted passes.
SPC core initialization occurs in the processor constructor, so the reported nodeNull abort occurs before the new player can instantiate its WASM core.
close() marks the player closed, aborts its initialization, releases any node and routing, then awaits context.close() for an owned context.
The temporary final-output guard replaces AudioNode destination connections with one zero-gain sink per context, connected with the original connect method; it does not wrap context.close/resume.
The aborted close-init player has not reached routing, so normal execution of that branch makes no destination connection and creates no final sink for the new context.
Prior successful playback contexts do acquire final zero-gain sinks that are not explicitly disconnected by the temporary guard; closed-context cleanup remains the browser engine responsibility.
The isolated original-binary close-init branch passed, while the full original-binary sequence failed earlier at its nonzero-playback assertion and never reached close-init.
plausibleHypotheses: An engine context/worklet lifecycle or state-reporting race while addModule is pending, potentially influenced by preceding playback and sample-rate context teardown.

The final-output interception changes prior graph/resource/timing conditions through persistent final GainNodes; no direct causal path from those prior sinks to the observed new context state was established.
